newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa will sell arms where it choses - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa will sell arms where it choses - Mandela.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela, rejecting a warning from the United Staes over a proposed arms deal with Syria, on Wednesday said South Africa would deal with which ever country it choses.
"We will conclude agreements with any country whether they are popular in the West or not. And that is what we likely to do in this case," Mandela told reporters at his home in Johannesburg.

The U.S. said on Monday it was extremely concerned by news of South Africa's proposed sale to Syria of aim-enhancing gear worth $641 million for its Soviet-made tanks, and threatened to cut off aid if the deal went ahead.

"We will never allow any support or assistance from any country, no matter how powerful it is, to dictate our foreign policy, nor allow any country to violate our sovereignty and undermine our national pride," Mandela said.

In what appeared on Tuesday to be a bid to back away from an arms deal with Syria, due to be discussed by the cabinet on January 22, the Foreign Ministry said no contract had been signed and any deal for what it termed "software" was not likely to be concluded before 1999.
Mandela however said the statement did not imply any question of backing down.
